bars:Line.name: Line
bars:Line.teaser: Europe's best bar of 2026 ferments its own fruit wines in a former Kato Petralona gallery
bars:Line.story: Line opened in 2022 in a former art gallery on a Kato Petralona backstreet, and it runs on the idea that almost nothing should leave the room as waste. The team ferments cloudy, live fruit wines it calls Why-ins with the winemaker Thanos Georgilas, brews its own beer and bakes sourdough, and the leftovers of one process feed the next. Behind it are Vasilis Kyritsis and Nikos Bakoulis, Greek World Class champions and founders of The Clumsies. Amsterdam crowned it Europe's best bar on 30 June 2026, and in Milan on 7 October the global ranking lifted it from No.8 to No.5.
bars:Line.why: Order a Why-in first: no other bar anywhere can pour it.
facts: A Kato Petralona backstreet, about ten minutes by taxi from Syntagma; no Acropolis view
A Why-in, Classic or Fancy, or the Delusional Margarita: reposado tequila, mustard, ketchup and potato water, improbably clean

bars:The Bar in Front of the Bar.name: The Bar in Front of the Bar
bars:The Bar in Front of the Bar.teaser: A pavement pop-up meant to hide scaffolding, now Europe's No.2 bar with eight new drinks a day
bars:The Bar in Front of the Bar.story: It was never meant to last. The team building Rumble in the Jungle, a jungle-themed room on Petraki, set a few stools on the pavement to screen the works, and the decoy outgrew the bar behind it. Alexandros Tselepis, Konstantinos Theodorakopoulos and Symeon Papanikolaou write a board of eight zero-waste cocktails every day from the prep leftovers inside, and the LED sign reading 'We serve humans too' has become a landmark of the lane. This year the European vote made it runner-up, and the global one put it 19th. There is no roof and not one indoor seat.
bars:The Bar in Front of the Bar.why: Let the bartender choose from today's board; by tomorrow it will have changed.
facts: Petraki lane by Syntagma; stools on the pavement, nothing indoors
Today's eight: zero-waste drinks on classic bones, with seasonal Greek fruit
A dry, still evening; in rain or a February wind it is not the same bar

bars:Baba au Rum.name: Baba au Rum
bars:Baba au Rum.teaser: The rum society that opened in 2009, before the Athens bar wave had a name
bars:Baba au Rum.story: Thanos Prunarus opened his 'rum and cocktail society' on Klitiou lane in 2009, a full bar generation before Athens filled the lists, and Greek press treats it as the cornerstone the modern scene grew from. Some four hundred rums line the back bar of a small room dressed in 1960s pop, and the crowd spills out onto the lane. The World's 50 Best organisation gave it the Legend of the List award in 2025, a year it sat 27th worldwide. This year's inaugural European ranking has it at No.14.
bars:Baba au Rum.why: Ask for a guided neat pour: the back bar is a lesson in rum, and the staff like teaching it.
facts: Klitiou 6, central Athens; the room spills onto the lane
The Supremus No.58: rum, falernum, cold tea and ripe summer fruit

bars:The Clumsies.name: The Clumsies
bars:The Clumsies.teaser: The 2014 bar that put Athens on the world list, pouring from morning coffee to past midnight
bars:The Clumsies.story: In 2014, deep in the Greek recession, Nikos Bakoulis and Vasilis Kyritsis persuaded three local backers to turn a run-down building on Praxitelous into an all-day bar. It entered the World's 50 Best Bars at No.22 in 2015, then held a top-ten place five years running to 2020, peaking at No.3; its founders later opened Line. Today it fills three floors, coffee in the morning and cocktails after midnight, with menus you can read only under UV light. It is no longer the insider find it was in 2017, but Europe's 2026 ranking still holds it at thirtieth.
bars:The Clumsies.why: Use it as the all-day address: coffee at ten, a gimlet at midnight, the same building.
facts: Praxitelous 30, central Athens, over three floors
The Mediterranean Gimlet: gin over a slow cordial of tomato water, cucumber, olive and oregano
Any hour: it opens for coffee in the morning and pours past midnight

bars:Barro Negro.name: Barro Negro
bars:Barro Negro.teaser: Greece's first agaveria, named for Oaxaca's black clay, now No.13 in Europe and No.40 in the world
bars:Barro Negro.story: Stelios Papadopoulos and George Kavaklis fell for Mexican agave and in 2019 opened what they call the country's first agaveria, naming it after the black Oaxacan clay a mezcal copita is shaped from. In about forty square metres at the edge of Klafthmonos Square they pour guided flights that move through smoke, wet clay, green agave and citrus, from a list Greece did not have before them. Their Academia de Barro Negro teaches Greek bartenders tequila and mezcal beyond the shot glass, with a study trip to Mexico in January 2025. In 2026 it ranked No.13 in Europe and No.40 in the world.
bars:Barro Negro.why: Let the bartender build you a flight; the room exists to change how you drink agave.
facts: The edge of Klafthmonos Square, in about forty square metres
A guided mezcal flight: smoke, wet earth, minerality

bars:Heteroclito.name: Heteroclito
bars:Heteroclito.teaser: The 2012 cave behind the cathedral where Greek natural wine found its first Athens glasses
bars:Heteroclito.story: Madeleine Lorantou and Dimitris Koumanis opened Heteroclito in 2012 in a small 1957 corner room behind the Metropolitan Cathedral, and it is widely credited as the centre's first dedicated natural-wine cave. The list is all Greek, about 200 labels, roughly four-fifths of them low-intervention, with some twenty poured as glasses, rotated monthly. Growers such as Kalathas, Ligas and Tetramythos built their Athens following here before they had distributors. There is barely a chair inside: most people stand out on the lane, cathedral bells behind them, over Greek cheese and charcuterie boards and Eastern Mediterranean plates.
bars:Heteroclito.why: It is a shop as well as a bar: carry a bottle back aboard at cave price.
facts: Fokionos 2 at the corner of Petraki, behind the Metropolitan Cathedral
A cloudy Tinos white from Domaine de Kalathas, Jérôme Binda's saline, orchard-wild island wine

bars:Tanini Agapi Mou.name: Tanini Agapi Mou
bars:Tanini Agapi Mou.teaser: Tannin, my love: about ninety Greek wines open by the glass on the Neapoli edge of Exarchia
bars:Tanini Agapi Mou.story: The name is a declaration: 'tannin, my love'. Since December 2018 this room on the quieter Neapoli side of Exarchia has kept around a hundred Greek wines, most from organic or biodynamic grapes, and about ninety of them are open by the glass, the deepest all-Greek pour in the city. Plants hang from the ceiling over birchwood tables by independent makers, and the staff wear no uniform. Culinary Backstreets called it 'the people's wine bar' in 2023, and chef Maria Kofitsa writes the small plates around whatever is in the glass. The cellar is Greek only, so save the Jura and the Loire for another night.
bars:Tanini Agapi Mou.why: Drink your way across Greece by the glass in one sitting, then take home the bottle you liked best.
facts: Ippokratous 91 at Methonis, on the Exarchia–Neapoli edge
Sotiris Koutroulis's skin-contact Malagousia, an Attica orange wine of apricot skin and dried herbs

bars:Alexander's Bar.name: Alexander's Bar
bars:Alexander's Bar.teaser: A stirred drink under an 18th-century Alexander tapestry, in the hotel partisans once mined
bars:Alexander's Bar.story: Efstathios Lampsas, a palace cook of peasant birth, founded the Grande Bretagne in 1874 on an 800,000-drachma loan. In the war the building served as Greek headquarters, then German, then British, and at Christmas 1944 EAM partisans, Manolis Glezos among them, packed the sewers beneath it with dynamite, then called the operation off when they learned Winston Churchill had just checked in. The bar sits on the ground floor facing Parliament: wood, leather, a walk-in humidor next door and, above the bottles, an authentic 18th-century tapestry of Alexander victorious at Gaugamela. Behind the counter, one of the city's deepest brandy cellars.
bars:Alexander's Bar.why: On a windy night choose this room over any rooftop: no view, but the most civilised drink in town.
facts: Ground floor of the Hotel Grande Bretagne, Syntagma Square, facing Parliament
A Negroni, or an old cognac from the brandy list, then a cigar chosen in the humidor next door
A cold or windy night, when the roofs lose their point

bars:The Line bars at the Athenaeum Inte.name: The Line bars at the Athenaeum InterContinental
bars:The Line bars at the Athenaeum Inte.teaser: A big hotel on Syngrou whose cocktail lists, by this guide's account, come from Europe's No.1 bar team
bars:The Line bars at the Athenaeum Inte.story: The grand hotels no longer set the Athens bar standard; some hire it. By this guide's July 2026 research, the team behind Line writes the cocktail lists at the Athenaeum InterContinental under a three-year collaboration, with drinks drawn from the hotel's art collection and poured in the lobby Artlounge, ToBar and Première, the rooftop with an Acropolis line of sight. A pianist plays the Artlounge on winter evenings; the roof works in the warm months. It is a large hotel on a busy avenue in Neos Kosmos, not a heritage room, and an October 2026 search found no public notice of the partnership, so ask at the bar.
bars:The Line bars at the Athenaeum Inte.why: Ask which drinks are Line's before you order; they are the reason to cross town.
facts: Syngrou Avenue, Neos Kosmos: the lobby lounges and the Première rooftop
A Line-built cocktail from the art-collection list, by the Artlounge piano or up on the roof
Winter evenings for the piano; warm-month nights for the rooftop

bars:A for Athens.name: A for Athens
bars:A for Athens.teaser: One drink for the straight-on Acropolis view above Monastiraki, then go drink somewhere else
bars:A for Athens.story: In the 2010s the two-level roof of this small design hotel on scruffy Miaouli street was the picture everyone took of the city's new bar scene: the Parthenon dead ahead across Monastiraki Square and a cocktail list themed on love, hope and realism. The scene has since moved down to street level and out to Petralona, and the drinks here now run second to the outlook. That is no reason to stay away. The reason to ride the lift is blue hour, when the floodlights come up on the Acropolis and the square fills below. Skip it on a hazy or windy day.
bars:A for Athens.why: Time it for blue hour, then leave the serious drinking to Klitiou lane or Petraki.
facts: Miaouli 2–4, beside Monastiraki metro, on the hotel roof
'Open Your Eyes': gin with ratatouille ketchup and tomato vermouth, savoury against the floodlit Parthenon
Blue hour, as the floodlights come up; not on a hazy or windy day

bars:Retsina — the revival bottle.name: Retsina — the revival bottle
bars:Retsina — the revival bottle.teaser: Pine resin, by law no more than one per cent, over the old Savatiano vines of the Mesogeia
bars:Retsina — the revival bottle.story: Retsina is the Attica native. Aleppo-pine resin goes into the must during fermentation, by law between 0.15 and 1 per cent, and the base is usually Savatiano, the drought-hardy grape of the Mesogeia plain about 30 km east of the city, where Markopoulo dates its wine records to 1831. Made with care, the pine reads as herb, not hardware. Domaine Papagiannakos of Markopoulo sets the modern benchmark; the Georgas family in Spata makes theirs natural and skin-contact; Kechris Tear of the Pine is the fine-dining bottle and Gaia Ritinitis Nobilis the easy way in. Drink it soon: airport and warehouse sprawl is eating the vineyards.
bars:Retsina — the revival bottle.why: Serve it cellar-cold beside taramosalata and the resin turns into seasoning.
facts: Pale and cellar-cold, pine as seasoning over Savatiano's baked apple and thyme
The word Retsina, Savatiano as the grape and Mesogeia (Mesogaia) as the place
Papagiannakos, Georgas, Kechris Tear of the Pine or Gaia Ritinitis Nobilis by name; refuse the tourist jug

bars:Ouzo, tsipouro, tsikoudia.name: Ouzo, tsipouro, tsikoudia
bars:Ouzo, tsipouro, tsikoudia.teaser: Three clear spirits, three different animals: read the label before the karafaki arrives
bars:Ouzo, tsipouro, tsikoudia.story: Athens keeps its spirits straight, and so should you. Ouzo is neutral spirit redistilled with anise; it turns milk-white the moment ice or water hits, because anethole will not dissolve in water, and EU law reserves the name for Greece and Cyprus. Plomari and Barbayanni, both from Lesvos, are the bottles to know. Tsipouro is distilled from grape pomace, so it keeps the fruit, and comes with or without anise: Tsililis from Thessaly, Idoniko from Drama. Cretan tsikoudia, also called raki, is pomace spirit too, single-distilled and never flavoured with anise.
bars:Ouzo, tsipouro, tsikoudia.why: Order a karafaki and a run of mezedes and sip slowly; nobody here takes it as a shot.
facts: Ouzo clouds white with water or ice; tsipouro and tsikoudia stay clear and taste of grape
Ouzo, a name only Greece and Cyprus may use; on tsipouro, whether it is made with or without anise
A karafaki of Plomari or Barbayanni ouzo, or Tsililis or Idoniko tsipouro, with a run of mezedes

bars:The grapes nobody else grows.name: The grapes nobody else grows
bars:The grapes nobody else grows.teaser: Assyrtiko, Xinomavro, and a white that nearly vanished before a professor handed over cuttings
bars:The grapes nobody else grows.story: The same revival that rescued retsina runs through grapes almost no one else grows. Assyrtiko comes off the volcanic soils of Santorini, taut and mineral. Xinomavro, from Naoussa in the north, is the acid-black red of Greece, built to age. Malagousia had all but disappeared until the 1970s, when Vassilis Logothetis, a professor in Thessaloniki, pressed cuttings on his student Evangelos Gerovassiliou, who brought the grape back into bottles; it is now planted across the country, Attica included. The pleasure of drinking Greek in Athens is that all three sit on the same list.
bars:The grapes nobody else grows.why: Taste all three side by side in one evening, then buy the bottle that surprised you.
facts: Assyrtiko taut and mineral; Xinomavro high-acid and dark; Malagousia aromatic and soft
Santorini PDO for Assyrtiko, Naoussa PDO for Xinomavro; Malagousia mostly under a regional name
A glass of each at Heteroclito, whose own card is in this fold

listening:Markos Vamvakaris.name: Markos Vamvakaris
listening:Markos Vamvakaris.teaser: A Syros stowaway vowed to learn the bouzouki in six months or cut off his hand. He kept the hand
listening:Markos Vamvakaris.story: Rebetiko, the Greek urban blues, took its classic shape after the 1922 refugee influx from Asia Minor; its harbour origins belong to the Piraeus guide. Markos Vamvakaris (1905–1972) left Syros at about twelve and worked from the bottom up: stevedore, coal carrier, the slaughterhouses, where he swore the vow. His first discs came in 1932, and around 1934 he formed the first bouzouki group to record and tour, with Batis, Delias and Pagioumtzis, moving the music out of the hash den and onto shellac. 'Frangosyriani', his 1935 song for a Catholic girl of Syros, became famous only in the early-1960s revival.
listening:Markos Vamvakaris.why: Ask the band for 'Frangosyriani': nearly every kompania in the city still builds its night on him.
facts: Klimataria on Plateia Theatrou, where house lore says he passed through; its own card is in the tables
The six-month vow survives only in his own telling

listening:Cloudy Sunday — Tsitsanis and.name: Cloudy Sunday — Tsitsanis and Bellou
listening:Cloudy Sunday — Tsitsanis and.teaser: Written under occupation, kept off record until 1948, and first sung with a defiant contralto
listening:Cloudy Sunday — Tsitsanis and.story: Vasilis Tsitsanis (1915–1984) wrote 'Synnefiasmeni Kyriaki' in occupied Thessaloniki in the shadow of the famine; the melody, he said, came out of the cloudy occupation. The studios were shut, so it reached shellac only in 1948, sung by Prodromos Tsaousakis with Sotiria Bellou. Bellou, born in 1921 near Chalkida, had arrived in wartime Athens with nothing, was heard by Tsitsanis, and from 1947 cut the 78s that made her rebetiko's defining contralto: flat, unornamented, refusing self-pity, and openly gay in 1940s Greece. Stelios Kazantzidis recorded the celebrated later version in 1959. Bellou died on 27 August 1997.
listening:Cloudy Sunday — Tsitsanis and.why: It is the one song a whole taverna will still sing unprompted; wait for the room to join in.
facts: Bellou's 1971 re-recording of Tsitsanis's 'Ta Kavourakia', the version crate-diggers chase
Accounts date the writing to 1943 or 1944; 'Ta Kavourakia' was first cut in 1952 by Takis Binis with Bellou, per the University of Ioannina archive

listening:1960 — the bouzouki at the Aca.name: 1960 — the bouzouki at the Academy Awards
listening:1960 — the bouzouki at the Aca.teaser: In one year a bouzouki tune went to the Academy Awards and a Ritsos poem became national music
listening:1960 — the bouzouki at the Aca.story: Manos Hadjidakis wrote the theme for Melina Mercouri in Jules Dassin's 'Never on Sunday' (1960), and on 17 April 1961, at the 33rd Academy Awards, it won Best Original Song, the first winner from a foreign-language film; its harbour scenes are told in the Piraeus guide. The same year Mikis Theodorakis set Yannis Ritsos's 1936 poem 'Epitaphios', and two rival recordings came out within weeks: Hadjidakis's refined orchestration sung by Nana Mouskouri, and Theodorakis's laiko version, Grigoris Bithikotsis singing over Manolis Chiotis's bouzouki. The Bithikotsis reading founded entechno, the moment rebetiko's instrument became national art music.
listening:1960 — the bouzouki at the Aca.why: Hear both Epitaphios records back to back: the argument over Greek music is all there.
facts: Play the two 1960 Epitaphios recordings in a row: Mouskouri for Hadjidakis, Bithikotsis for Theodorakis

listening:Kapnikarea.name: Kapnikarea
listening:Kapnikarea.teaser: Unamplified rebetiko at table height in a Byzantine church's shadow, from mid-afternoon, all year
listening:Kapnikarea.story: In 1977 Sotiris Sofos, a tailor from Ikaria, set tables beside the Byzantine church of Kapnikarea. Ermou became a pedestrian street in 1996, and his son Dimitris has since let a rotating pool of about twenty-five musicians work the alley most afternoons from around 14:30: rebetiko without amplifiers, played at table height, with no stage and no set list. When the winter rooms go dark from June to September, this is the surest place in the centre to hear the music, and in daylight at that.
listening:Kapnikarea.why: Arrive just before half past two and let lunch run into the second hour of music.
facts: Christopoulou 2 at Ermou 57, beside the Kapnikarea church
Music most afternoons from about 14:30, all year (seen Jul 2026)
A small per-head music charge on the bill (seen Jul 2026)

listening:Klimataria.name: Klimataria
listening:Klimataria.teaser: The 1927 taverna under the vine where the kompania starts late and plays from memory
listening:Klimataria.story: For the music, come to Klimataria late on a music night, when the band plays from memory among the wine barrels and the room keeps the zeibekiko's time with its palms. Its own card, kitchen and all, is in the tables.
listening:Klimataria.why: Book a music night and come hungry: the band starts late and the pots carry you there.
facts: Barrel wine by the kilo jug and a plate of soutzoukakia
Music nights from about 22:30; the venue record says Wednesday to Saturday, but other listings differ, so call
About EUR 20–35 a head, more on music nights (seen Jul 2026)

listening:The winter rooms.name: The winter rooms
listening:The winter rooms.teaser: Two storied rebetiko rooms that play only in the cold months, neither yet confirmed for 2026–27
listening:The winter rooms.story: The rebetiko circuit's best-loved rooms are winter rooms, shut through the summer until October. In Ano Petralona, Giorgos Xintaris has held a Friday residency at Mousiki Skini Hamam, running October to May. In the Varvakios arcade, Stoa Athanaton on Sofokleous 17–19 was still singing in 2026, but under a shifting name. A search in October 2026 found no published 2026–27 programme for either, so treat both as a phone call, not a promise. If they answer, these are the nights to plan a week around; if not, Kapnikarea and Klimataria play all year.
listening:The winter rooms.why: Ring before Friday: a winter room that answers is worth rebuilding the whole evening around.
facts: Call from October; neither room's 2026–27 season was confirmed in October 2026
Stoa Athanaton trades under a shifting name, so check what it is called this winter

listening:Half Note Jazz Club.name: Half Note Jazz Club
listening:Half Note Jazz Club.teaser: Athens' serious jazz room for more than forty years, a Mets club that goes dark every summer
listening:Half Note Jazz Club.story: Half Note on Trivonianou in Mets has been the city's serious jazz room for more than four decades, the club the rest of the scene orbits. Its 2025–26 season brought the guitarist Gilad Hekselman and the Stavros Lantsias Octet. It closes every summer and for Easter week, so a July visitor misses it; in early summer the city's jazz moves outdoors instead, to the free Athens Jazz festival at Technopolis. In mid-October 2026 the new season's programme had not yet surfaced in search, so check the club's own listings before planning a night around it.
listening:Half Note Jazz Club.why: Choose the night by the artist, not the date: the booking is the whole point.
facts: Trivonianou 17, Mets, near the Panathenaic Stadium
Autumn to late spring; closed in summer and Easter week. The 2026–27 programme was unconfirmed (Oct 2026)
Through the club's own listings at halfnote.gr

listening:Lena Platonos — Gallop.name: Lena Platonos — Gallop
listening:Lena Platonos — Gallop.teaser: A 1985 record of analog synths, a drum machine and spoken poems that collectors now hunt
listening:Lena Platonos — Gallop.story: Lena Platonos made 'Gallop' in 1985 with analog synthesizers, a Roland TR-808 drum machine and her own surreal spoken poetry, and it sounded like nothing else in Greek music at the time. It found a second life in 2015, when the San Francisco label Dark Entries reissued it on vinyl, and international crate-diggers began to treat her as the Athenian name to hunt. Set beside the bouzouki story of this fold, it is the other Athens: private, electronic and strange, the city talking to itself late at night.
listening:Lena Platonos — Gallop.why: Play it after a night of rebetiko and hear how far one city travelled in a generation.
facts: The 2015 Dark Entries vinyl reissue; ask for it by name in the city's record shops

listening:Hi-fi — the one listening room.name: Hi-fi — the one listening room
listening:Hi-fi — the one listening room.teaser: One listening room this guide can vouch for, and an honest word about the rest
listening:Hi-fi — the one listening room.story: A listening bar is a room where the sound system and the records are the point and the drinks follow. This guide can stand behind one in Athens: the vinyl booth at Okupa in Kerameikos, which takes over from the laptops in the evening; its own card is under Rooms to linger & work. An October 2026 search turned up other names in online listings and a hi-fi showroom offering booked sessions, but none confirmed by the venue or the quality press for 2026, so none is recommended here. If you find one, judge it by ear.
listening:Hi-fi — the one listening room.why: Go to Okupa for the records; treat any other 'listening bar' as unproven until you have heard it.
facts: Okupa's vinyl sessions, Tuesday to Sunday evenings; its own card is in Rooms to linger & work
